observation.description: Every semantic refusal an application handler raises collapses to the single generic diagnostic code SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED. The arm's documented conflict semantics (compare-and-move: 'stale move: revision 2, expected 1'), an already-consumed invite, and a validation failure are indistinguishable at the code level — a client that wants to branch on 'stale move → refetch and rebase' versus 'invite consumed → show error' must parse prose message text. The host's own refusals are exemplary (uniform coded SNAPBACK_AUTH_PERMISSION_DENIED, SNAPBACK_STANDARD_PATTERN_CURSOR_INVALID, etc.); application semantics get no equivalent vocabulary.
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a3-snapback-web/evidence/scenario-evidence.json (A3-08 loserRefusal: code SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED, message 'stale move: revision 2, expected 1')
demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a3-snapback-web/evidence/app/acceptance.a3.mjs (A3-08 reconciliation branch keyed on message text)

competitorOutcome.description: Convex application errors carry a developer-defined ConvexError with structured data the client can switch on (official docs); the frozen 0102 arms similarly branched on app-defined error payloads rather than message strings.

mustNotRegress: The terminal, non-catchable character of host-owned denials (auth denials must never be maskable by app error vocabulary), and the uniform non-disclosing shape of negative responses.
smallestCoherentFix: A declared application refusal channel: handlers throw a typed refusal (code from a declared closed set plus a JSON-safe details payload validated like a result contract); the envelope carries it as diagnostic.appCode beside SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED so existing consumers keep working.
acceptanceWitness: A mutation declares refusals: ['STALE_MOVE'] and throws it; the client observes diagnostic.appCode === 'STALE_MOVE' with typed details, while an undeclared throw still surfaces as plain SNAPBACK_HANDLER_FAILED.
